admission_decision: establish fine-grained true Rust default daemon admission only; keep dae run, install, release, dae-wing, and daed on the Go-backed default until every row passes with matched evidence

admission_rows.current_blocker: current release/package smoke builds the Go dae artifact and Stage 22 live evidence uses opt-in helpers, not a Rust default daemon identity
admission_rows.next_action: define the Rust daemon artifact identity, CLI compatibility surface, version output, and explicit Go fallback selector before any default mutation
admission_rows.required_evidence: a real Rust daemon binary or Rust-owned dae run entrypoint starts the default daemon without relying on the Go daemon as the active runtime owner

admission_rows.current_blocker: config helpers exist, but default daemon admission has not proven full validate/export parity under the installed dae CLI contract
admission_rows.next_action: build a shared corpus for valid, invalid, permission-denied, subscription, geodata, and export cases before enabling Rust default validation
admission_rows.required_evidence: Go and Rust validate/export produce matched fixtures, diagnostics, default paths, permission handling, and failure messages for the same config corpus

admission_rows.area: startup, pid, progress, and systemd notify
admission_rows.current_blocker: package smoke verifies the Go-backed service fields only; no Rust default daemon has emitted the pid/progress/systemd ready protocol
admission_rows.next_action: run isolated Rust daemon startup smoke with service-compatible paths and compare progress bytes and readiness timing against Go
admission_rows.required_evidence: OnReady, sdnotify ready, /var/run/dae.pid, /var/run/dae.progress, startup cleanup, pprof lifecycle, and dry runtime semantics match daenew

admission_rows.current_blocker: Stage 22 live evidence proves selected active path behavior, but the Go engine still owns the daemon lifecycle and control-plane swap
admission_rows.next_action: port and validate newControlPlane lifecycle ownership before treating Rust helpers as the default daemon
admission_rows.required_evidence: Rust owns control-plane construction, subscription resolution, persist cleanup, resolver setup, reload loop, runtime resources, and bounded shutdown

admission_rows.current_blocker: Stage 22 active TCP evidence is opt-in and does not prove a Rust-owned default daemon can carry the production TCP path
admission_rows.next_action: run TCP live traffic through the Rust default daemon candidate and record packet path, dial target, mark, mptcp, latency, and fallback evidence
admission_rows.required_evidence: true Rust default daemon passes tproxy/eBPF TCP traffic with sniffing, route result lookup, RouteDialTcp reroute, MagicNetwork mark/mptcp, and outbound relay parity

admission_rows.current_blocker: Stage 22 UDP/DNS evidence is opt-in and does not prove Rust owns endpoint pool, DNS controller, or domain map lifecycle by default
admission_rows.next_action: run UDP, DNS UDP/53, must-rule UDP/53, cache migration, and endpoint pool live smoke under the Rust default daemon candidate
admission_rows.required_evidence: true Rust default daemon passes UDP endpoint pool, UDP/53 DNS controller path, DNS upstream MagicNetwork, cache restore, domain_routing_map owner tracking, and sendPkt reply parity

admission_rows.current_blocker: current contracts do not prove Rust can own bpfObjects, map-in-map writes, flip handles, and cleanup through default daemon reloads
admission_rows.next_action: add kernel owner admission smoke covering load, attach, EjectBpf, InjectBpf, Close, reload rollback, and stale resource cleanup
admission_rows.required_evidence: map ABI, pinned map reuse, listen socket map keys, tc/netns/sysctl attach order, mprog/netkit fallback, cleanup order, and root/capability errors match daenew

admission_rows.current_blocker: Stage 22 reload rollback evidence is local opt-in evidence; Rust default daemon has not proven old listener and BPF ownership survival
admission_rows.next_action: run success, invalid-config rollback, suspend, abort, repeated reload, and concurrent reload smoke under the Rust default daemon candidate
admission_rows.required_evidence: reload progress bytes, SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2, abort marker, listener reuse, DNS same-bind stop, EjectBpf/InjectBpf rollback, old path survival, and suspend no-load semantics match daenew

admission_rows.current_blocker: Stage 22 validates in-process evidence, but daed/dae-wing-facing default daemon telemetry and API route behavior are not admitted
admission_rows.next_action: compare Go vs Rust RuntimeOverview JSON, HTTPTransport dial targets, subscription fetches, and route-aware DNS behavior before downstream product rollout
admission_rows.required_evidence: RuntimeOverview samples, DNS stats, UDP task telemetry, route-aware Engine HTTPTransport, subscription/bootstrap direct, and MagicNetwork mark/mptcp remain visible to WebUI/API consumers

admission_rows.current_blocker: Stage 17 through Stage 21 keep multiple protocols and shared transports in helper or contract state, including QUIC/H3, REALITY, xHTTP, gRPC, Meek, Mux, Vision, and Trojan-Go paths
admission_rows.next_action: complete protocol-level true dataplane gates before using any Rust daemon as the production default
admission_rows.required_evidence: all default outbound protocols and shared transports pass parser, handshake, true dataplane, live traffic, reload cleanup, benchmark, and rollback gates

admission_rows.current_blocker: Stage 22 benchmark is no-daemon direct baseline vs opt-in candidate active-proxy, not a Go default daemon vs true Rust default daemon comparison
admission_rows.next_action: create a benchmark harness that starts both daemon identities with the same config, traffic matrix, corpus, and measurement windows
admission_rows.required_evidence: matched Go default daemon vs true Rust default daemon latency, throughput, RSS, CPU, startup, reload, UDP/DNS, and protocol traffic benchmarks on the same corpus and host

admission_rows.current_blocker: product chain admission is defined but cannot roll forward until true Rust daemon identity and dataplane parity are admitted
admission_rows.next_action: keep all default mutations denied and record every row result before reopening product-chain switching
admission_rows.required_evidence: Go fallback selector, opt-in/opt-out controls, package/systemd rollback, release artifact labeling, config rollback, and downstream product rollback are documented and smoke-tested

denied_default_mutations: do not switch dae run default engine to Rust
do not replace control.NewControlPlane default owner with a Rust owner
do not mutate install/dae.service ExecStart to a Rust-only daemon
do not label release assets as Rust-default-daemon-ready
do not update dae-wing or daed defaults from dae-local evidence alone
do not remove Go outbound or Go daemon fallback
name: stage23-true-default-daemon-admission
required_benchmarks: Go default daemon vs true Rust default daemon TCP proxy latency and throughput on matched loopback traffic
Go default daemon vs true Rust default daemon UDP proxy and DNS UDP/53 latency, loss, and throughput on matched traffic
Go default daemon vs true Rust default daemon outbound protocol benchmarks for every admitted protocol
RSS, CPU, startup time, reload time, and post-reload resource cleanup comparison on the same host
benchmark evidence must include raw logs, command lines, config corpus, host/kernel metadata, and rollback result
rollback_controls: keep Go-backed dae binary and service path available during all true Rust daemon experiments
require an explicit opt-in selector for every Rust daemon candidate run
write all daemon candidate state under temporary test paths unless a rollout record explicitly allows otherwise
kill only the candidate process on failed smoke and leave the installed daemon untouched
restore old control-plane ownership on reload failure before reporting admission success
record validation and benchmark evidence in the local plan before changing any gate state
